sum: BeOne announced on November 26 that it had reached a new commercialization agreement with Novartis for Tafinlar and Mekinist. Under the agreement, BeOne will handle the exclusive importation, commercial promotion and distribution of both medicines in mainland China, excluding Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, according to VCBeat.

The arrangement takes effect on December 1, 2026. Tafinlar contains dabrafenib and Mekinist contains trametinib; the two medicines are used together in targeted oncology treatment. GMAB Stock Soars 71% in 3 Months on Pipeline Progress & Sales Growth
sum: Genmab GMAB shares surged 71% over the past three months compared with the industry’s 1.9% growth. The rally has been driven by a series of encouraging late-stage clinical developments across the company's oncology pipeline, along with strong revenue growth in the first nine months of 2026.

The company develops antibody-based therapies for cancer and other serious diseases. Its marketed cancer treatments include Epkinly/Tepkinly for certain types of B-cell lymphomas and Tivdak for cervical cancer (HNSCC). Genmab's late-stage pipeline is led by petosemtamab for head and neck and colorectal cancers and Rina-S for ovarian and endometrial cancers. In addition to product sales, Genmab generates substantial royalty revenues from partnered medicines, including Johnson & Johnson's Darzalex and Novartis' Kesimpta.
Genmab's recent stock rally has been supported by encouraging late-stage results for its two key investigational candidates, petosemtamab and Rina-S, across multiple cancer indications.

In late October, Genmab announced positive data from the phase III LiGeR-HN1 study evaluating petosemtamab, an investigational bispecific antibody, in combination with Merck's MRK Keytruda (pembrolizumab) in patients with first-line recurrent or metastatic HNSCC. Merck's Keytruda is an established PD-1 inhibitor approved across multiple cancer types.

The study met both primary endpoints of overall survival (OS) and objective response rate, regardless of HPV status. The combination reduced the risk of death by 50% compared with Keytruda alone, demonstrating a meaningful survival benefit. These encouraging findings strengthen petosemtamab's potential as a treatment for HNSCC and bring the candidate closer to potential regulatory discussions. Petosemtamab is also being tested in a separate late-stage study for second- and third-line recurrent/metastatic HNSCC patients.

Notably, in the same month, Genmab entered into a clinical trial collaboration with Incyte INCY to evaluate a new combination therapy for the first-line treatment of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) carrying the KRAS G12D mutation. The combination will include INCB161734, Incyte’s investigational KRAS G12D inhibitor, petosemtamab, and standard chemotherapy.

European healthcare stocks have solidified their safe-haven status amid doubts about AI
sum: Steady profit growth and demand for key drugs are making the European healthcare sector a safe haven from the volatility of AI companies' stocks, according to Bloomberg
European healthcare companies have exceeded forecasts for the 11th consecutive quarter / Photo: Mahir Asadli / Shutterstock

Against the backdrop of growing uncertainty surrounding investments in artificial intelligence, the “defensive appeal” of European healthcare stocks is on the rise, Bloomberg noted. In the third quarter, companies in this sector posted their strongest earnings growth in two years, the agency notes, emphasizing that their actual results have exceeded expectations for 11 consecutive quarters. As a result, these companies’ earnings per share are also rising, Bloomberg observes.

Earnings per share for companies in the MSCI Europe Health Care Index (which tracks the performance of large- and mid-cap companies in the healthcare sector across 15 developed European countries, including shares of Roche, Novartis, AstraZeneca, Novo Nordisk, GSK, Sanofi) rose 13% in the third quarter—the fastest pace for that period in the last two years—while analysts had expected growth of only 2.4%, according to Bloomberg. More than 71% of companies in the sector exceeded earnings forecasts.

Moreover, the growth was widespread: pharmaceutical companies’ revenue in the third quarter rose 8.4% compared with an expected 7%, while profits for medical equipment manufacturers and healthcare service providers increased by 11% against a forecast of 4.1%, according to data from Bloomberg Intelligence (BI). AstraZeneca’s profits exceeded analysts’ estimates thanks to strong growth in its oncology division, while high demand for biosimilars and services at its hospitals helped Germany’s Fresenius beat expectations. Companies with a significant share of sales in the U.S. also benefited from the strengthening dollar, Bloomberg reports.

France's Sanofi, which generates about half of its revenue in the U.S., has raised its sales and profit forecasts twice amid growing demand for Dupixent, its best-selling drug for treating skin conditions and asthma.

sum: Novartis agreed a new China commercialization arrangement with BeOne Medicines on November 26, according to Gosset. BeOne will exclusively import, promote and distribute Novartis medicines dabrafenib, marketed as Tafinlar, and trametinib, marketed as Mekinist, across mainland China.

The arrangement excludes Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. It takes effect on December 1, 2026, and extends BeOne's role beyond designated broad-market regions covered by the companies' earlier cooperation.

For Novartis, the agreement changes the commercial route for two established oncology products in one of the industry's largest pharmaceutical markets. BeOne will handle importation, commercial promotion and distribution, while Novartis retains ownership of the medicines.

The agreement gives BeOne responsibility across the mainland market rather than only selected broad-market areas. The source says the two medicines have four approved indications in China and are included on the national reimbursement list.

The development is relevant to investors because it reshapes the regional commercialization model for an established oncology franchise. The announcement does not disclose financial terms, so its direct earnings effect cannot be quantified from the reported agreement.

Novartis Faces $16.7 Billion Patent Cliff After 2030 as CEO Challenges
sum: Novartis has moderated its long-term sales growth outlook amid expected revenue declines from key medicines facing patent and pricing pressures. The company believes its existing brands and development pipeline can help offset these losses, while analysts remain more cautious about future performance. The outlook highlights the importance of new drug launches, pipeline execution and portfolio diversification in sustaining pharmaceutical growth.
Novartis Projects a $16.7 Billion Sales Decline from Three Blockbusters by 2035 and Tells Investors the Street Is Too Pessimistic

The cliff is quantified, and the company is open about it. Kisqali, Cosentyx and Kesimpta are projected to fall from $23.9 billion in 2030 to $7.2 billion in 2035, a $16.7 billion drop, with Kisqali declining most, from $11 billion to $2.9 billion, and with US exclusivity for Kisqali ending in the second half of 2031 under patent settlements. By our calculation, the three-drug decline is about 70%, and Kisqali’s is about 74%. Novartis itself calls 2026 the largest loss-of-exclusivity impact in its history, and Spherical Insights reports that Entresto will shed roughly $4 billion of sales this year.

The guidance is slightly lower, and the CEO’s argument is about the gap. The new target is about 5% annual growth at constant currency for 2026–2031 against 5% to 6% for 2025–2030, with a core operating margin above 40% by 2029, though the CFO said margin should dip at least two points in coming years. Analysts model 2035 sales at roughly $64 billion, about $20 billion below the mid-single-digit path, and Narasimhan answered that if that gap is real “then your probabilities are wrong,” adding that “it just takes two or three of these to hit, and you get there.” He said most 2031–2035 growth would come from internally developed medicines, and that guidance assumes no large acquisition.
The company points to raised peak-sales targets and a deep pipeline.

items.t: Novartis stock: ORION-4 shows cardiovascular benefit for Leqvio
sum: Novartis reported positive topline results from the Phase III ORION-4 trial on Monday, November 23, 2026. According to the company's Novartis media release, the study met its primary endpoint and showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events when Leqvio was added to standard lipid-lowering treatment.

ORION-4 provides the first cardiovascular outcomes evidence for Leqvio, also known as inclisiran, in patients with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. The trial evaluated whether twice-yearly treatment could reduce events such as coronary heart disease death, myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke and urgent coronary revascularization.

More than 16,000 participants were randomized to receive inclisiran or placebo on the first day, after three months and then every six months. Novartis said the findings support the potential of sustained LDL cholesterol reduction through a healthcare-provider-administered treatment.

Full ORION-4 results are planned for publication in the first half of 2027. The company said ORION-4 and the ongoing VICTORION-2 PREVENT trial together form one of the largest advanced lipid-lowering cardiovascular outcomes programs in secondary prevention, with more than 33,000 participants enrolled across the two studies.

Novartis stock traded at 139.27 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:42 CET on Monday, November 23. The result adds a new clinical outcome signal to the company's longer-term case for Leqvio, although the full dataset and publication will provide the next material detail for investors.

items.t: Novartis CEO rejects claims AI will cure cancer within a decade
sum: Novartis Chief Executive Vas Narasimhan has challenged claims that artificial intelligence could cure cancer within five to 10 years, arguing that the technology’s impact on drug development will be more gradual than some industry leaders expect.
Narasimhan, who also serves on the board of AI developer Anthropic, told the Financial Times that even substantial improvements in research efficiency would take time to produce new treatments.

His assessment contrasts with the optimism expressed by Anthropic Chief Executive Dario Amodei, who has suggested that increasingly powerful AI could dramatically compress the time required for scientific discoveries.
Narasimhan said it could take a decade to reduce the drug-development process by about four years.
AI is already being used in pharmaceutical research to identify promising compounds, analyze biological information and improve clinical trial design.
However, successful drug development also requires laboratory experiments, human trials, regulatory approval and evidence of safety and effectiveness.

Novartis is expanding its use of AI across research, manufacturing and commercial operations, while maintaining that technological advances will not eliminate the scientific and regulatory challenges involved in bringing medicines to patients.

Novartis stock sets 5% sales growth target through 2031
sum: On November 19, Novartis said in an ad hoc announcement that it expects net sales to grow at a 5% compound annual rate at constant currencies from 2026 through 2031. The Swiss drugmaker also said its core operating income margin is on track to return to above 40% by 2029.

Novartis raised its peak sales outlook for three marketed medicines. Kesimpta, used in multiple sclerosis, now has a peak sales target of USD 8 billion, up from USD 6 billion. The company lifted its forecasts for leukemia treatment Scemblix and cholesterol medicine Leqvio to USD 5 billion each from USD 4 billion.

The changes build on a previous increase for Rhapsido, also known as remibrutinib, whose peak sales potential was raised to USD 8 billion across chronic spontaneous urticaria, chronic inducible urticaria and relapsing multiple sclerosis. Novartis said nine in-market assets now have peak sales potential between USD 3 billion and USD 10 billion.

The company said more than 35 potentially submission-enabling readouts are expected through 2031. Its pipeline contains more than 30 potential high-value assets across cardiovascular-renal-metabolic medicine, immunology, neuroscience and oncology. More than 20 are in registration, Phase II or Phase III, while more than 10 are in or entering Phase I.

Novartis presented the outlook at its Meet Novartis Management event in London. Chief Executive Vas Narasimhan said the upgraded brand forecasts, together with the broader portfolio, support the expectation of sustained mid-single-digit sales growth over the longer term. The company also highlighted efforts to scale artificial intelligence across research, development, manufacturing and commercial operations.

The announcement gives investors a clearer view of how Novartis intends to offset major loss-of-exclusivity effects while its newer medicines expand. The stronger forecasts for Kesimpta, Scemblix and Leqvio improve the contribution expected from products already on the market, but the longer-term plan still depends on successful clinical development, regulatory submissions and launches.

Novartis stock: FDA approves Cosentyx for polymyalgia rheumatica
sum: On November 17, Novartis said in a company press release that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Cosentyx (secukinumab) 150 mg for adults with polymyalgia rheumatica, or PMR. The indication covers patients who have responded inadequately to corticosteroids or cannot tolerate a corticosteroid taper.

Cosentyx is the first and only anti-interleukin-17 biologic approved in the United States for PMR, according to Novartis. The decision expands the medicine's U.S. label to 11 indications and gives physicians an option beyond prolonged steroid treatment in a disease that can cause pain and stiffness in the shoulders, neck and hips.

The FDA decision was based on the Phase III REPLENISH trial, a randomized, double-blind study conducted across 27 countries. Participants received Cosentyx at 150 mg or 300 mg, or placebo, alongside a 24-week steroid taper.

At week 52, sustained remission was achieved by 40.5 percent of patients receiving the 150 mg dose, compared with 20.5 percent of those receiving placebo. Novartis said the trial also evaluated complete sustained remission, cumulative steroid exposure and the time to escape or rescue treatment.

The reported safety profile remained consistent with the established Cosentyx profile. Serious adverse events occurred in 15.9 percent of patients in the 150 mg group and 14.2 percent in the placebo group. Hypersensitivity reactions occurred in 14 percent and 9 percent, respectively, while urinary tract infections occurred in 13 percent and 7 percent.

Novartis said the PMR indication is already approved in the European Union and that regulatory reviews are continuing in additional markets, including Japan. The company also said it had filed the REPLENISH results for review in Japan and other countries.
Novartis stock traded at 143.76 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:52 CET on Wednesday, November 18.

Novartis stock: FDA weighs tumor-risk action for gene therapies
sum: On November 6, 2026, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration said it was investigating a serious malignancy risk linked to Novartis' gene therapies Zolgensma and Itvisma. The FDA safety communication said the review follows postmarketing reports of tumors in patients treated with Zolgensma.

The agency said three cases involved tumors associated with the GLI1 oncogene. In two cases, molecular analysis showed that DNA from the Zolgensma vector had integrated into the patients' genomes, with the construct inserted upstream of or within GLI1. The mechanism behind GLI1 overexpression in the third case remains under investigation.

The reports involved tumors in the central and peripheral nervous systems, spinal and paraspinal regions, and the kidney. The FDA said the risk applies to both onasemnogene abeparvovec products because Zolgensma and Itvisma use the same vector and construct. No neoplasia cases had been reported after Itvisma administration as of the agency's communication.

The FDA said the overall benefits of both therapies continue to outweigh their potential risks for approved uses. It is nevertheless evaluating whether regulatory action is appropriate and reviewing the adequacy of current prescribing information and Novartis' long-term follow-up safety studies.

Both products' U.S. prescribing information describes a theoretical risk of tumorigenicity from integration of AAV vector DNA into the genome. In the meantime, the agency said patients and clinical trial participants receiving the therapies should be monitored for tumor formation. The review creates a regulatory and safety issue for Novartis' gene-therapy portfolio, while the FDA's benefit-risk statement leaves the products' approved uses unchanged for now.

Novartis stock traded at 144.90 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:32 CET on Friday, November 13. Investors will watch the FDA's assessment of product labeling and long-term monitoring requirements alongside the company's pipeline updates.

sum: The US Food and Drug Administration is investigating a serious malignancy risk linked to Novartis' Zolgensma gene therapy for spinal muscular atrophy. A safety alert dated Saturday, November 7, 2026, and published by the Hong Kong Department of Health reproduces the FDA's findings. Novartis stock traded at 145.84 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:43 CET on Thursday, November 12, 2026.

The FDA said postmarketing reports involved tumors in the central and peripheral nervous systems, spinal and paraspinal areas, and the kidney. Three cases involved the GLI1 oncogene, which can promote cancer when overexpressed or abnormally activated.

In two cases, molecular testing found that Zolgensma's adeno-associated virus vector DNA had integrated into the patients' genomes. The therapy's promoter was positioned upstream of or within GLI1. The mechanism behind GLI1 overexpression in a third case remains under investigation.

The agency said the identified risk applies to Itvisma as well as Zolgensma because the products use the same vector and genetic construct. No neoplasia cases had been reported after Itvisma treatment at the time of the alert. The FDA is also monitoring comparable adeno-associated virus programs.

The FDA is assessing whether changes are needed to the prescribing information or to long-term follow-up requirements for the two products. Novartis is conducting long-term safety studies. Patients and clinical-trial participants receiving either therapy should be monitored for tumor formation.

The safety issue adds a regulatory overhang to Novartis' gene-therapy portfolio, although the FDA said the overall benefits of Zolgensma and Itvisma continue to outweigh their potential risks for approved uses. The review does not itself announce a label change, withdrawal or restriction.

On the bottom line, Legend remained in the black after posting its first profit in Q2, recording an adjusted net income of $56 million in Q3, slightly down from $63 million in the three months ending in June.

Despite Carvykti’s growth momentum, Legend’s CFO Carlos Santos warned investors on a conference call Tuesday that Wall Street’s current sales consensus for 2027 sits “at the higher end of the scenarios that we’re currently anticipating.” Even though he said that double-digit year-over-year growth is still expected for the BCMA CAR-T next year, the more conservative projection likely put a damper on investor sentiment.
Santos attributed Legend’s reservation to launch delays outside the U.S. and, perhaps more alarming to investors, “a slower earlier-line share growth in the U.S.”

Investors have been concerned about Carvykti’s prospects in earlier multiple myeloma treatment settings because of competition from off-the-shelf bispecifics, including the BCMAxCD3 T-cell engager Tecvayli made by J&J.

Back in the second quarter, Legend’s stock price fell 10% after J&J’s then-innovative medicine chief, Jennifer Taubert, described the Tecvayli-Darzalex combo as having “the potential for cure” in second-line multiple myeloma.

Novartis Confirms Zolgensma Caused Tumors in Two Children Via Gene Therapy Vector Integration
sum: Nine tumor reports in SMA gene therapy patients reveal a risk the drug's FDA label still calls theoretical — raising urgent questions about post-market surveillance and what families of 6,000-plus treated children should do now

If your child received Zolgensma for spinal muscular atrophy, here is what you need to know today: Novartis has confirmed that the gene therapy's viral vector integrated into the DNA of two treated children and caused tumors — a risk the company's own prescribing information still describes as "theoretical" and says has not been causally established. The FDA label has not been updated to reflect these confirmed cases. Talk to your child's neurologist about whether tumor surveillance is warranted, particularly if your child was treated one to five years ago.

Novartis disclosed Thursday that nine children who received its blockbuster SMA gene therapy Zolgensma have since been diagnosed with tumors. In two of those cases, pathological analysis found direct evidence that the gene therapy's adeno-associated virus (AAV) delivery vehicle had inserted itself into a patient's chromosomes — a process called insertional mutagenesis — and that this integration event was the likely cause of the tumor. Both confirmed patients received treatment for their tumors and are continuing to be monitored.

The disclosure, confirmed by STAT News, confirmed by BioSpace, reported by Endpoints News, and the SMA UK National MDT safety update dated November 4, 2026, is the first confirmed case of insertional mutagenesis causing tumors in patients treated with a commercially approved gene therapy. The confirmation also reveals a critical gap in the drug's existing prescribing information: Section 5.6 of Zolgensma's FDA label still states that "a causal relationship with ZOLGENSMA has not been established" — language that is now factually incorrect.
Novartis shares (NYSE: NVS ADRs) fell Thursday as investors weighed the implications for one of the company's most high-profile branded medicines.

Since Zolgensma's U.S. approval in May 2019, Novartis has received nine reports worldwide of tumors arising in previously treated patients. Of those nine reports, three children's tumors underwent pathological testing.

Novartis Shares Slide After Neuromuscular Candidate Acquired with Avidity Fails Phase III Trial
sum: Novartis shares fell the most in a single day since the COVID-19 pandemic after the pharma giant acknowledged that its neuromuscular candidate delpacibart etedesiran (del-desiran) failed a pivotal Phase III trial assessing the antibody oligonucleotide conjugate (AOC) in patients with myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1).

Del-desiran failed the Phase III HARBOR trial (NCT06411288) by missing the study’s primary endpoint of statistically significant improvement vs. placebo in video Hand Opening Time (vHOT) through week 54. vHOT is a frequently used measure of hand myotonia, according to a 2024 study, and involves clinical experts reviewing videos to measure the time from hand grip to opening.

However, Novartis added that it saw evidence of clinical activity in exploratory analyses and secondary endpoints—which included hand grip strength and quantitative Muscle Testing composite score, both measured by dynamometer; MD1 activity and participation scale; and 10-Meter Walk/Run Test. Safety findings from HARBOR were generally consistent with previously reported data, according to Novartis.

Novartis did not disclose details of its data but said it is evaluating the full dataset from the HARBOR trial and will engage with authorities to determine the most appropriate development path for del-desiran.

“Developing therapies for a complex disease like DM1 remains challenging, and setbacks are part of scientific progress,” Shreeram Aradhye, president, development and chief medical officer, Novartis, said in a statement. “As we continue to evaluate the full HARBOR dataset, we remain committed to identifying the most appropriate development path for the del-desiran program and advancing innovative approaches for people living with DM1 and other serious neuromuscular diseases.”

Del-desiran’s failure marked Novartis’ third clinical setback in a week. On Friday after the closing bell, the company and partner Ionis Pharmaceuticals acknowledged that their co-developed pelacarsen failed the Phase III Lp(a)HORIZON trial (NCT04023552) by missing its primary endpoint of reducing the risk, compared with placebo, of cardiovascular events—a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, and urgent coronary revascularization requiring hospitalization.

Novartis stock falls nearly 4% as heart-drug failure deepens setbacks
sum: Novartis suffered a second trial disappointment within a week, after the Swiss pharma group’s potential blockbuster heart drug failed in a final-stage study.

The drug, pelacarsen, did lower levels of lipoprotein(a), a largely genetic risk factor for cardiovascular disease that affects roughly one in five people. However, that reduction did not translate into fewer deaths, heart attacks and strokes compared with placebo, the Swiss drugmaker said late on Sept 4.

The failure marks a major setback to hopes the medicine would open up a new approach to preventing cardiovascular disease. It also comes just days after Novartis temporarily paused trials of an experimental cell therapy for autoimmune diseases after three patients died.

Novartis shares fell as much as 3.9 per cent on Sept 7 in early Zurich trading, the biggest decline in over four months. They have gained 14 per cent so far this year. Amgen, which is developing a similar heart drug, fell almost 7 per cent in post-market trading on Sept 4.

“This questions whether any Lp(a)-lowering therapies can ultimately show a cardiovascular benefit,” according to Michael Leuchten, an analyst at Jefferies. Any negative reaction might be overstated, as even a successful trial would have raised questions over which patients would benefit and how well the drug could compete, he added.

Novartis is counting on a string of new medicines to sustain growth when some of its biggest products lose patent protection. Chief executive officer Vas Narasimhan has said successful late-stage trials could allow the company to raise its forecast for 5 to 6 per cent annual sales growth till 2030.

Analysts had seen pelacarsen as a potential blockbuster, with peak sales estimates ranging from about US$1.5 billion (S$1.9 billion) at UBS to US$5.4 billion at Jefferies, though the investment bank assigned the drug just a 30 per cent probability of success. Novartis had pegged the overall market opportunity at more than US$5 billion.

items.t: Novartis AG Stock (NVS) Moved Down by 3.14% on Jun 1: Key Drivers Unveiled
sum: Novartis AG (NVS) moved down by 3.14%. The Pharmaceuticals & Medical Research sector is down by 1.67%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Eli Lilly and Co (LLY) down 1.75%; Revolution Medicines Inc (RVMD) down 0.60%; Pfizer Inc (PFE) down 1.74%.

Novartis (NVS) experienced a decline in its share price today amidst a backdrop of mixed news and broader market pressures. While the company recently delivered encouraging updates regarding its pipeline, these positive developments appear to have been overshadowed by other factors.

Investor sentiment on the day was generally cautious, partly influenced by escalating geopolitical concerns related to a U.S.-Iran conflict, which led to a broader market downturn. Such macroeconomic and geopolitical events can often trigger significant intraday volatility and impact even fundamentally strong companies.

Adding to this, Novartis had recently announced early data from an experimental actinium-based radiopharmaceutical drug showing promising anti-tumor activity in prostate cancer. However, analysts also cautioned about the management of side effects, specifically high rates of dry mouth and severe anemia, which could introduce an element of risk regarding the drug's future development and adoption. This mixed assessment of a key pipeline asset may have contributed to investor unease.

Furthermore, upcoming domestic policy discussions in Switzerland, where Novartis is based, could be influencing investor sentiment. A looming referendum that proposes capping the country's population has reportedly caused alarm within the tech and pharmaceutical sectors, potentially signaling future operational challenges for companies reliant on international talent.

Earlier in the year, the company's first-quarter 2026 earnings indicated a miss on earnings per share forecasts, though revenue exceeded expectations. While Novartis later updated its full-year sales and profit guidance upwards, the initial earnings report, coupled with ongoing analyst discussions that present a range of price targets and recommendations, may still be contributing to uncertainty among some investors.

sum: New Cosentyx® (secukinumab) data from REPLENISH, largest ever global Phase III trial in polymyalgia rheumatica, to be highlighted in oral session

Basel, June 1, 2026 – Novartis will present new data from 31 abstracts across its industry-leading immunology portfolio at the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) Congress on June 3-6 in London, advancing scientific insight into high-burden autoimmune diseases.

"Novartis is committed to shaping the future of immunology. From small molecules to biologics and CAR-T cell therapy, our pioneering science is focused on where we can have the greatest impact on patient outcomes," said Angelika Jahreis, Global Head, Immunology Development, Novartis. "At EULAR, we will share compelling new data for Cosentyx, ianalumab and our CAR-T therapy rap-cel across diseases where there is high unmet need. These data demonstrate how Novartis innovation can have meaningful impact for people living with autoimmune diseases like polymyalgia rheumatica, Sjogren's disease, systemic lupus erythematosus and systemic sclerosis."
